Guides

What to check before you hire someone for IT help

Hiring someone to work on your computers or network means giving them access to your private information. Ask these questions first.

Ask for a clear quote. A good provider explains what is included before starting. Be cautious about vague or open-ended pricing.

Ask who will do the work. You should know exactly who is coming to your home or business.

Ask about warranty or follow-up. What happens if the problem comes back? Get the answer in writing.

Ask about your data. Will they back up your files first? How will they handle passwords and private information?

Do not rely on claims you cannot check. If someone says they are certified, licensed or insured, it is fair to ask for proof.

Look for plain language. You should understand what is being done and why. Good help does not hide behind jargon.

Get notes afterwards. Ask for a summary of what was changed, and keep any passwords somewhere safe.

Trust your gut. If you feel rushed or pressured, step back.
